dimensions.label: Paragraph load
dimensions.explanation: Measures paragraph volume and its upper tail. High volume is a review signal, not a defect or an instruction to shorten.
limitations: Paragraphs can legitimately sustain an argument across many words.

dimensions.label: Sentence load
dimensions.explanation: Measures sentence volume and its upper tail. Long sentences are review signals, not automatic errors.
limitations: Sentence splitting is heuristic.
Length is a surface proxy; it does not establish comprehension.

dimensions.label: Fragmentation
dimensions.explanation: Detects excessive fragmentation as well as excessive density. Section-opening transitions are excluded from the score.
limitations: Intentional staccato passages exist.
Dialogue and list-heavy chapters may need profile-specific treatment.

dimensions.label: Rhythm
dimensions.explanation: Measures paragraph-length spread and repeated construction. A narrow band can reveal an artificially mechanical edit.
limitations: Rhythm is partly rhetorical; no metric can prescribe the correct variation.
Very short chapters do not provide enough paragraphs for a stable estimate.

dimensions.label: Lexical accessibility

limitations: Flesch formulas were not designed for technical vocabulary and proper names.
A higher score is not automatically better; precision can require difficulty.
